batches.theme: Returned A04 reconstructions: cordage topology and compass-to-map relationship
batches.relationship: Rope crossing order (over/under) that defines each knot; baseplate, dial, needle and neat line in one ground frame

plates.returned_reason: A04: drawn cord crossing and terminal dot did not establish a dressed bowline; sketch withdrawn.
plates.physical_relationship: Loose bowline: overhand loop with the working side on top, end up through the loop, behind the standing part and back down; tail and overhand stopper inside the fixed loop; short-tail failure view.
plates.source_basis: K14 FM 3-97.61 (Aug 2002) 4-12 Bowline tying steps and checkpoints, pages 4-13 to 4-14; independent standard-bowline crossing diagram (Wikimedia Commons File:Bowline (standard).svg, CC BY-SA 3.0) used only to cross-check crossing order; card tying sequence.
plates.construction: Computed by scripts/build_w2c_knots.py from a depth model rendered by scripts/w2c_rope.py.
plates.geometry_validation: qa/KNOT_TOPOLOGY.json: bowline core crossing order equals the reference sequence O1 U2 U3 O4 O5 U6 O2 U7 U5 O6 U1 O7 O3 U4; stopper is an alternating three-crossing overhand (isolated determinant 3); tail end inside the fixed loop (FM checkpoint 2); minimum depth gap 1.8, minimum crossing angle 45 degrees; failure view keeps the same core.
plates.inspection: Inspected at 900, 390 and 360 px and in grayscale: five numbered stages sit beside the strands they name, crossings stay distinct without colour, failure panel reads by glyph and text. Page and print context in context/ and proofs/.
plates.card_changes: Cites new claim K14 for the tying, backup and inspection steps; corrected the inspection sentence (the collar hugs the standing part and the small loop grips the two strands); caption describes the new plate.
plates.remaining_dependencies: Rigging safety and field education review of depicted topology and stopper choice; physical tying check; current TC 3-97.61 wording.

plates.returned_reason: A04: two-colour zigzag weave merged a stopper with a loop; withdrawn pending independently checked topology in two views.
plates.physical_relationship: Two separate knots: a figure-eight stopper in a line end bearing on a tarp grommet under pull; a figure-eight loop in doubled cord whose two strands run side by side without crossing.
plates.source_basis: K15 FM 3-97.61 (Aug 2002) 4-14 figure-eight knot description and 4-20 Figure-eight loop checkpoints, pages 4-15 and 4-21 to 4-22; card text for the grommet use (editorial).
plates.construction: Computed by scripts/build_w2c_knots.py; the loop strands are offsets of the verified figure-eight core.
plates.geometry_validation: qa/KNOT_TOPOLOGY.json: stopper and loop core each have four alternating crossings and determinant 5 (the only knot of crossing number at most 4 with determinant 5 is the figure-eight); doubled loop has exactly four strand crossings per core crossing, matching depth order, and no strand-on-strand crossing (FM 4-20 checkpoint 2).
plates.inspection: Inspected at 900 px and in grayscale: grommet relationship and pull direction visible, loop strands parallel, labels clear of strands and plate edges.
plates.card_changes: Cites new claim K15 for the knot structure steps; caption describes the two views.
plates.remaining_dependencies: Rigging safety and field education review; physical check that the depicted stopper bears on a typical tarp grommet; current TC 3-97.61 wording.

plates.returned_reason: A04: compass and meridian shown separated; neither the instruments' relationship nor the correction applied was shown.
plates.physical_relationship: Plan view in a fixed true-north frame: baseplate edge on the map neat line with the dial set from map north and corrected for an exaggerated east declination; after turning map and compass together the red needle overlays the orienting arrow and map north points to true north; two landmark sight lines through map symbols.
plates.source_basis: N14 USGS How To Get Your Map and Compass To Face the Same Direction (orientation steps); N08 and T08 NOAA NCEI Magnetic Declination (east positive; true = magnetic + declination); N03 USGS topographic map FAQ for terrain association.
plates.construction: Computed by scripts/build_w2c_navigation.py from one angular model with a reusable compass component.
plates.geometry_validation: qa/NAVIGATION_GEOMETRY.json: in both panels the travel arrow is parallel to the neat line, the orienting arrow equals travel plus declination and the needle points to magnetic north; only the oriented panel has the needle in the arrow and map north on true north; north keys draw the same 12 degree angle, labelled as exaggerated. Tolerance 0.15 degree for 0.1 px coordinates.
plates.inspection: Inspected at 900 px: compass enlarged so the needle and orienting arrow relationship is legible; maps clipped to their panels; labels clear of map content.
plates.card_changes: First action now follows the USGS step order (baseplate on a neat line, dial to map north, declination correction unless an adjustable compass is already set) and cites N14; landmark and rotation actions cite N14; caption describes the plate.
plates.remaining_dependencies: Navigation and search and rescue review; confirm instrument-specific conventions for adjustable-declination compasses; current local declination values are not depicted.

batches.theme: Household water and wastewater flow paths
batches.relationship: Where water moves, under what pressure, and where contamination enters or is stopped

plates.physical_relationship: Supply pressure drop draws liquid from a submerged hose end back through the hose and faucet into house pipes; a hose-bibb vacuum breaker venting to air, an air gap above the rim, and no hard connection to rain barrels, sumps or untreated pumps stop it.
plates.source_basis: U21 EPA Cross-Connection Control Manual (EPA 816-R-03-002, Feb 2003): Chapter 3 page 12 and Figure 7 (backsiphonage, submerged inlet); Chapter 4 page 16 (air gap) and page 18 (hose bibb vacuum breaker); case history of a garden hose in a pesticide barrel back-siphoned during a service interruption (page 8).
plates.construction: Generated by scripts/w2c_plates_b02.py with shared primitives in scripts/w2c_svg.py.
plates.geometry_validation: Reverse-flow arrows follow the hose and house pipe toward the pressure drop in the main; air arrows enter the vacuum breaker vents; the hose end is shown above the rim. No numeric geometry. Chromium label audit: 0 clipped, 0 overlaps.
plates.inspection: Inspected at 900 px, then in the reader at 390 and 1280 px and in Letter and A4 proofs (A4 in grayscale); labels clear of parts and plate edges.
plates.card_changes: Actions and verify cite new claim U21; caption describes the two panels.
plates.remaining_dependencies: Licensed plumber and drinking-water safety review; local plumbing code governs device selection.

plates.physical_relationship: Advisory tap water enters the refrigerator supply line, passes through the filter cartridge and feeds the icemaker and door dispenser; reservoirs are filled from safe water instead of the tap.
plates.source_basis: W07 and D12 CDC Drinking Water Advisories: An Overview (Mar 4, 2024): do not drink or use water from appliances connected to the water line, including refrigerator water and ice dispensers; boil water that has passed a home filter during a boil advisory. P12 NCHFP: freezing does not kill all pathogens. Reservoir and flushing statements are not covered by that page (see W2C-E007).
plates.geometry_validation: Flow arrows follow the supply line to the filter, icemaker and dispenser; crosses sit on the icemaker, dispenser and advisory tap. No numeric geometry. Label audit clean.
plates.inspection: Inspected at 900 px, then in the reader at 390 and 1280 px and in Letter and A4 proofs (A4 in grayscale); labels clear of parts and plate edges.
plates.card_changes: Caption describes the cutaway; the CDC page does not cover post-advisory flushing, so the plate ends at utility clearance (see W2C-E007).
plates.remaining_dependencies: Drinking-water public health review of reservoir and flushing guidance; appliance manufacturer instructions.

plates.physical_relationship: Groundwater in saturated soil presses up on the base of an emptied septic tank, lifting it from its seat and breaking inlet and outlet joints; a full, unopened tank stays seated while basement drains are plugged, water use is cut and equipment stays off the wet drainfield.
plates.source_basis: U07 EPA Septic Systems - What to Do after the Flood (last updated Aug 24, 2026): do not pump during flooded or saturated drainfield conditions; pumping could cause the tank to try to float out of the ground and may damage the inlet and outlet pipes; plug basement drains and drastically reduce water use; do not compact the soil absorption field with equipment; professional inspection and servicing.
plates.geometry_validation: Load arrows act upward on the tank base; the original seat is dashed below the lifted tank; breaks are drawn at both pipe joints. No numeric geometry. Label audit clean.
plates.inspection: Inspected at 900 px, then in the reader at 390 and 1280 px and in Letter and A4 proofs (A4 in grayscale); labels clear of parts and plate edges.
plates.remaining_dependencies: Onsite wastewater engineering review; tank buoyancy depends on site and system.

plates.physical_relationship: With no power the submersible pump cannot run or refill the pressure tank; the tank pushes out only its small stored reserve before the tap sputters; stored drinking water, a labelled pump breaker and licensed contractors form the plan.
plates.source_basis: U22 MDH Well Owner's Handbook (4th ed., updated Jan 2014) page 16 Pressure Tanks: the tank supplies water when the pump is not running; a pressure switch starts and stops the pump; common 20- to 44-gallon tanks have a drawdown of 5 to 16 gallons. U08 Ready.gov: at least 1 gallon per person per day. U06 MDH and U02 CPSC: licensed contractors for well and electrical work.
plates.geometry_validation: No flow arrows in the unpowered well; low gauge reading on the tank; dashed power line from the unpowered breaker to the pump. The drawdown range is quoted from MDH and labelled as typical. Label audit clean.
plates.inspection: Inspected at 900 px, then in the reader at 390 and 1280 px and in Letter and A4 proofs (A4 in grayscale); labels clear of parts and plate edges.
plates.card_changes: First action cites new claim U22; stage labels no longer state an unsupported brownout breaker rule; caption describes the cross-section. The verify line still asks that the pump stay off during brownouts, which no cited source supports (W2C-E008).
plates.remaining_dependencies: Licensed well contractor and master electrician review, including any brownout guidance.

plates.physical_relationship: Labelled non-potable water is poured into the toilet bowl and flushed only into a working sewer or septic line; drinking and food water stay on a separate shelf; gurgling, slow drains, odour or backup stop all flushing in favour of a lined bucket toilet.
plates.source_basis: U07 EPA septic flood page: do not use the system while the soil is saturated or flooded. U13 CDC: lined bucket toilets with heavy bags and tight lids when sewer service is unusable; keep non-potable water from drinking and food uses.
plates.geometry_validation: Flow arrows run from the bucket into the bowl and down the drain to the sewer; the separation line keeps drinking water apart. No numeric geometry. Label audit clean.
plates.inspection: Inspected at 900 px, then in the reader at 390 and 1280 px and in Letter and A4 proofs (A4 in grayscale); labels clear of parts and plate edges.
plates.card_changes: Stage labels replace the unsupported 24-hour storage limit with the observable stop signs; caption describes the section. The verify line still contains the 24-hour limit (W2C-E009).
plates.remaining_dependencies: Environmental health review; local health department rules for alternate flushing water.

batches.theme: Combustion products and fuel vapours in occupied spaces
batches.relationship: Where carbon monoxide or fuel vapour comes from, where it collects in a building, where warning devices sit, and the exit

plates.physical_relationship: CO from an open gas oven, a charcoal grill and a camp stove fills a closed room and reaches a sleeper; a cracked window does not clear it; the alternative is warm layers in one interior room and early relocation.
plates.source_basis: C22 CPSC Carbon Monoxide Questions and Answers (gas ranges and ovens not for heat; charcoal never indoors; camping equipment indoors only if designed for it); C16 CDC CO basics; C05 CPSC camping equipment; U25 Ready.gov Power Outages (no gas stove or oven for heat; go to a community location with power).
plates.construction: Generated by scripts/w2c_plates_b03.py with shared primitives in scripts/w2c_svg.py.
plates.geometry_validation: Air arrows rise from each source into the CO region that contains the sleeper; the window is drawn cracked open. No numeric geometry. Label audit clean.
plates.inspection: Inspected at 900 px, in the reader at 390 and 1280 px, and in Letter and A4 (grayscale) batch proofs; labels clear of parts and plate edges after layout fixes.
plates.card_changes: Actions cite new claims C22 and U25; caption describes the room section.
plates.remaining_dependencies: Fire service and CO safety review; CPSC allows camping equipment designed for enclosed spaces, while the card forbids all camp stoves indoors.

plates.physical_relationship: Smoke and CO alarms on every level including the basement, a CO alarm outside the bedrooms, none in the kitchen or directly above the furnace, with replacement rules.
plates.source_basis: C22 CPSC CO Q&A (every level and outside sleeping areas; not in kitchens, above fuel-burning appliances or near vents; test button checks circuitry not sensor accuracy; replacement age from the manufacturer); U04 Ready.gov Home Fires (smoke alarms on every level including the basement; replace units every 10 years or per manufacturer; batteries twice a year unless 10-year lithium).
plates.geometry_validation: One smoke and one CO alarm per level; crossed CO alarms mark the kitchen and furnace exclusions. No numeric geometry beyond the sourced 10-year smoke alarm rule. Label audit clean.
plates.inspection: Inspected at 900 px, in the reader at 390 and 1280 px, and in Letter and A4 (grayscale) batch proofs; labels clear of parts and plate edges after layout fixes.
plates.card_changes: First action cites C22; stage labels replace the unsupported monthly-test and 5-10 year CO lifespan with sourced rules; caption describes the cutaway. Card actions still state inside-bedroom smoke alarms, monthly tests and CO lifespans that the cited pages do not support (W2C-E013).
plates.remaining_dependencies: Fire prevention and CO safety review; NFPA placement rules for smoke alarms inside bedrooms need a primary source.

plates.physical_relationship: Scaled outage plan: generator outdoors at least 20 ft from windows, doors and the attached garage with exhaust pointed away; LED lanterns, closed refrigerator and freezer, unplugged electronics and a CO alarm inside.
plates.source_basis: U25 Ready.gov Power Outages (generators, camp stoves and charcoal grills outdoors at least 20 ft from windows, doors and attached garages; CO detectors on every level; refrigerator about 4 h and full freezer about 48 h when closed; unplug against surges; community location in extreme heat or cold); C06 CPSC generator release (at least 20 ft, exhaust away).
plates.construction: Generated by scripts/w2c_plates_b03.py; plan drawn at 6 px per foot with a scale bar.
plates.geometry_validation: Builder check measures from the SVG: 6.0 px/ft from the scale bar; wall face to generator 20.0 ft; garage to generator 42.3 ft (both at least 20 ft).
plates.inspection: Inspected at 900 px, in the reader at 390 and 1280 px, and in Letter and A4 (grayscale) batch proofs; labels clear of parts and plate edges after layout fixes.
plates.card_changes: Two actions cite U25; caption describes the scaled plan. U01 still claims flashlights instead of candles, but its page does not mention candles (W2C-E012).
plates.remaining_dependencies: Emergency management and electrical/CO review; the plan shows minimum clearance, not a safe distance in all wind conditions.

plates.physical_relationship: Gasoline vapour from basement cans stays low and travels across the floor to a water-heater pilot flame; sealed approved cans and an upright cylinder belong in a ventilated outdoor shed away from the home.
plates.source_basis: U24 CPSC Consumers Warned Against Storing Gasoline (July 30, 1979): heavier-than-air vapours travel to ignition sources such as stove and furnace pilot lights; keep cans outdoors away from living quarters and ignition sources, such as in a well-ventilated shed; never store gasoline in the house. Propane storage rests on card text (W2C-E015).
plates.geometry_validation: The vapour band hugs the floor from the cans to the pilot; the storage arrow leads away from the home to the shed. No numeric geometry. Label audit clean.
plates.inspection: Inspected at 900 px, in the reader at 390 and 1280 px, and in Letter and A4 (grayscale) batch proofs; labels clear of parts and plate edges after layout fixes.
plates.card_changes: Two actions cite U24; stage labels drop the unsupported 6-12 month rotation; caption describes both panels.
plates.remaining_dependencies: Fire prevention and hazardous-materials review, including propane cylinder storage and local fire-code limits.

plates.physical_relationship: A user with a clear escape route behind them sprays the base of a fire confined to one pan; PASS steps; smoke filling the room, spread beyond one object or no way out means leaving and calling 911.
plates.source_basis: U23 USFA Choosing and Using Fire Extinguishers (last reviewed Apr 1, 2023): use only when others are alerted, the fire department is called, the user is able, the fire is small and contained to one object such as a pan or wastebasket, the user is safe from smoke and has a clear escape route; PASS steps.
plates.geometry_validation: The spray arrow ends at the base of the flame; the exit door is behind the user. No numeric geometry. Label audit clean.
plates.inspection: Inspected at 900 px, in the reader at 390 and 1280 px, and in Letter and A4 (grayscale) batch proofs; labels clear of parts and plate edges after layout fixes.
plates.card_changes: All lines now cite U23 alongside U04; the third stage label shows the depicted leave conditions. The water-on-grease warning in the first action has no supporting source yet (W2C-E016).
plates.remaining_dependencies: Fire service review; a primary source for the grease-fire and electrical-fire water warning.

batches.relationship: Where to be in a building, who a warning device reaches, how warning areas are drawn, and how fast floodwater rises

plates.physical_relationship: Floor plan: leave large open rooms and the glass storefront for the designated shelter or an interior room on the lowest floor; vehicles are not safe, so no one goes to the parking lot.
plates.source_basis: D22 NWS What to do During a Tornado (At Your Workplace or School: follow the drill to the shelter location, stay away from windows, avoid large open rooms such as cafeterias, gymnasiums or auditoriums; vehicles are not safe); D03 same page.
plates.geometry_validation: Motion arrows lead from the open room to the interior core; crosses mark the open room, glass and vehicle. No numeric geometry. Label audit clean.
plates.inspection: Inspected at 900 px, in the reader at 390 and 1280 px, and in Letter and A4 (grayscale) batch proofs; label collisions fixed before acceptance.
plates.card_changes: Lines cite new claim D22; caption describes the plan. The first action still claims wide-span roofs are the first to collapse, which the NWS page does not state (W2C-E019).
plates.remaining_dependencies: Emergency management and structural safety review; building-specific shelter plans govern.

plates.physical_relationship: An outdoor siren reaches a person outside but is not designed to wake people inside a closed house; a bedside NOAA Weather Radio and phone alerts sound the warning in the bedroom.
plates.source_basis: D23 NWS Quad Cities Outdoor Warning Sirens FAQ (sirens are designed only to alert those who are outside; every home and business should have a NOAA Weather Radio); T15 NWS NOAA Weather Radio; T14 Ready.gov alerts.
plates.geometry_validation: Solid sound arcs reach the outdoor person; dashed weakened arcs stop at the house wall; alert arcs come from the bedside radio. No numeric geometry. Label audit clean.
plates.inspection: Inspected at 900 px, in the reader at 390 and 1280 px, and in Letter and A4 (grayscale) batch proofs; label collisions fixed before acceptance.
plates.card_changes: Two actions cite new claim D23; caption describes the plate.
plates.remaining_dependencies: Meteorology and emergency communications review; local siren policies vary.

plates.physical_relationship: A broad multi-county watch area where conditions are favorable, and a storm-based warning polygon around the threat path that includes a town ahead of the storm, independent of county lines.
plates.source_basis: D24 NWS Flood Warning VS. Watch (watch = favorable; warning = imminent or occurring; advisory = nuisance); D25 NWS Storm Based Warnings fact sheet (polygons since October 1, 2007, not restricted to county boundaries).
plates.geometry_validation: The warning polygon lies inside the watch area, crosses county lines and contains the town on the storm motion vector. No numeric geometry. Label audit clean.
plates.inspection: Inspected at 900 px, in the reader at 390 and 1280 px, and in Letter and A4 (grayscale) batch proofs; label collisions fixed before acceptance.
plates.card_changes: Two actions cite D24 and D25; the third stage label now describes the depicted polygon instead of the undepicted Emergency tier; caption updated.
plates.remaining_dependencies: Meteorology review; Emergency-tier definitions need their own primary source (W2C-E020).

plates.physical_relationship: Schematic water level against time: a flash flood rising rapidly within about 6 hours of its cause, and a river flood rising toward a forecast crest as the river overtops its banks; ice jams and dam or levee failures can release a sudden flood.
plates.source_basis: D26 NWS Flood Related Hazards (flash floods generally develop within 6 hours of the immediate cause; rapid rise; ice jams; dam or levee failure with little warning); D24 NWS (flash floods can take minutes to hours and can occur where it is not raining).
plates.geometry_validation: Curves have no time scale; the flash flood curve rises steeply right after the rain bars and both peaks exceed the marked flood level. The river curve is schematic (W2C-E021). Label audit clean.
plates.inspection: Inspected at 900 px, in the reader at 390 and 1280 px, and in Letter and A4 (grayscale) batch proofs; label collisions fixed before acceptance.
plates.card_changes: Two actions cite D24 and D26; caption describes the schematic curves.
plates.remaining_dependencies: Flood hydrology review; a primary source for river-flood lead times and crest forecasts.
